text:
Ellie (docs): Quick sync — I'm updating the Export examples in the retention docs and want to align CSV headers with the UI and SDKs. Proposed CSV header change: replace `user_id` with `pseudonymized_identifier`, add `retention_policy_id`, and rename `ttl` to `expiry_timestamp`. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/987

Marco (eng-privacy): Sounds reasonable. One ask: can we avoid 'identifier' implying reversible id? Prefer `pseudonymized_identifier` or `hashed_subject_id`? We pseudonymize using HMAC with a per-tenant key.

Sofia (legal): +1 on 'pseudonymized_identifier'. Please add a short blurb in docs: "Pseudonymized identifiers are irreversible hashes produced with tenant-scoped keys; re-identification requires key access." Keeps our SOC2 wording clearer.

Olivia (product): FYI product UI currently exposes the header names as `data_ttl_days` in the export. If docs change to `expiry_timestamp` we need to ship a tiny UI rename or add an alias mapping on export.

Ava (devex): I can update SDK snippets to do header mapping. Proposed Python snippet:

```
# map export CSV headers to SDK fields
HEADER_MAP = {
  'pseudonymized_identifier': 'subject_hash',
  'retention_policy_id': 'policy_id',
  'expiry_timestamp': 'expiry_ts'
}
```

I'll include the snippet in the PR under "SDK mapping examples".

Marco (eng-privacy): Also add a one-liner about key rotation: rotated keys will yield different pseudonymized values; make sure teams know to keep mapping tables if they expect stable hashes across rotations.

Ellie (docs): Good catches. I'll update the PR: change header names to `pseudonymized_identifier`, add the CSV example row and the legal blurb from @Sofia, and include the Python mapping snippet from @Ava. I'll also add a small note about UI aliasing for `data_ttl_days` and link a follow-up ticket for product.

Olivia (product): Ticket created: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/PRJ-4213/docs-export-field-aliasing

Ellie (docs): Thanks — will push an amended commit today and request reviews from @Sofia and @Marco. 

deploy-bot: PR 987 opened by ellie/docs — reviewers requested: sofia (legal), marco (eng-privacy).

Olivia (product): Quick thumbs up from product on phrasing; prefer 'expiry_timestamp (RFC3339)' in examples.

Ellie (docs): Noted, will use RFC3339 in example rows.

Marco (eng-privacy): Small nit: in the blurb, prefer 'irreversible pseudonymization' instead of 'irreversible hashes' for lay readers.

Ellie (docs): Good call — updated wording in branch. Last message here; merging after legal + privacy review.
